text:
maria: Quick q — thinking about adding a 'safety sanity' final stage in the model onboarding pipeline. Runthrough: full safety/eval suite (toxicity, privacy checks, hallucination heuristics). Pro: catches bad releases. Con: slow + expensive. @kevin any thoughts on block vs flag behavior?
kevin: Blocking by default is risky. At scale we'll be queuing thousands. Maybe block only on 'high severity' consensus. Otherwise auto-flag + require human in the loop. :thinking:
oliver: +1 for severity thresholds. Practical rule: block if >=3 different high-severity alerts across independent test families (e.g., toxicity, privacy, instruction-following), measured on a curated probe set. Example: >=3/50 prompts with score>0.8 => block.
reza: Cost perspective — full suite per-import is expensive. Proposal: multi-tiered approach: fast preflight (100 prompts, classifier heuristics) on every PR; full-safety (1k prompts, ensemble checks) for major model or major weight changes; nightly sampled full runs for new models. CLI stub: `run_onboard --preflight --samples 100` / `run_onboard --safety-full --samples 1000`.
amy: Ops constraints: Dedicated overnight jobs ok but for Private deployments need to ensure KMS/HSM keys are available for telemetry encryption. Also we must store eval artifacts (inputs, model outputs, scores) in the model entry so QE can reproduce issues.
maria: Good, so multi-tier + block-on-severity consensus + artifacts stored. I'll draft RFC with gating thresholds & sample probe sets. Any objections to blocking rule being '>=3 high signals across 3 families'?
kevin: No objections. One caveat: define 'high' rigorously (e.g., toxicity score>=0.9 or PII exact match).
oliver: Also add a 'fast rollback' automation: if post-deploy monitoring sees spike in customer-incident signals, auto-rollback to previous pinned model.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled safety-run queued for model 'maria/demo_fin-2024-06' at 2024-06-15T03:00Z — env=dedicated-nightly
maria: Thanks all — will post RFC link when ready. :+1:
